pattern.top_pattern: Authorization coding and facility mapping issues are inflating apparent spend
pattern.what_is_impacting: Authorization coding and facility mapping in CA / NY / CO
pattern.pattern_details: A meaningful share of the reported increase is tied to authorization-code movement and facility records landing in unmapped buckets, so this is a gating validation issue before any policy or provider action. CA drives the largest auth-code shift, NY shows the same pattern, and CO plus CA also show spend flowing through Not Mapped facility classifications. The business risk is acting on what may be data movement rather than real utilization or reimbursement change.
pattern.why_it_matters: If this is not cleaned up first, downstream UM, reimbursement, and network actions may target the wrong drivers.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Run a joint UM operations and data-quality reconciliation on PA-required coding and facility mapping for CA, NY, and CO, then restate the impacted segments before changing policy or provider strategy.
pattern.validation_reason: Both auth-code distribution shifts and unmapped facility buckets are explicitly flagged as requiring validation before action.
evidence_summary: CA authorization-code distribution accounts for +$3.4M and is flagged for validation before action.
NY shows another +$0.7M from authorization-code distribution shifts.
CO PPO Not Mapped facility spend adds +$0.6M on 17 more admissions while paid per admit fell, pointing to classification movement rather than price.
CA Not Mapped facility buckets add about +$0.6M across HMO and PPO, concentrated at UC IRVINE MEDICAL CENTER.
